newsitem.title: USA: Continental Airlines sees "very good" Q4.
newsitem.headline: Continental Airlines sees "very good" Q4.

text.p: Continental Airlines Inc said Wednesday that it expects a "very good" fourth quarter, after reporting third quarter earnings of $0.25 per share after charges earlier in the day.
Chief Executive Gorden Bethune said in a conference call with reporters that the company's "booking trends look very good" and the company is "expecting a very good fourth quarter."
He declined to be more specific.
Analysts estimate Continental will post fourth quarter earnings of $0.54 per share, compared to $0.55 a share last year, according to First Call.

Continental officials also said they have hedged their fuel through mid-February to protect themselves from rising fuel costs, which attributed to a 1.9 percent rise in costs per available seat mile during the third quarter.

Separately, Bethune said Continental should reach a definitive agreement with Air France in the next two weeks. Earlier on Wednesday, the company said it signed a code sharing agreement with Air France to link schedules. Delta also linked with Air France.

Continental also said it will expand its pact with with Alitalia. The expanded agreement will allow it to start two new flights to Rome and one to Milan next summer. The agreement is awaiting governmental approvals, Continental said.
The company said it had a cash balance of $865 million at the end of the quarter, compared with $603 million for the year-ago period.
